title: Twin
description: The structured form every error a conforming provider produces arrives in (RFC §5.1.1). No raw stderr, driver message, or bare stack trace is ever the primary error the agent sees; an error the provider has not structured is still a twin, with code `UNSTRUCTURED` and the raw message in `received` (RFC §5.1.4). The twin is also the mid-failure discovery path: its `comprehendo` field tells an agent that never probed that the fluent path exists (RFC §4.4).

comprehendo.description: The spec version this provider implements, e.g. "0.1". Self-identifying (RFC §4.4).

code.description: The provider's stable, machine-readable error code (SCREAMING_SNAKE by convention). Left as a plain string on purpose: RFC §11 puts twin code vocabularies in the provider's hands, not this spec's, so the schema types the field and never polices the value. Once published, a code MUST NOT change meaning.

reason.description: One sentence, plain language, stating WHY. MUST be self-sufficient: an agent reading only `reason` and `fixes` can act without consulting anything else.

path.description: Where in the input the problem is, e.g. "pipeline[2].$grup".

namespace.description: The provider-defined scope the error concerns: a collection, a file, a subcommand.

declared.description: What the input claimed, or what a valid form looks like. Untyped in the RFC (`unknown` in TypeScript, `Any` in Python), so untyped here.

received.description: What actually arrived. Untyped in the RFC. For an `UNSTRUCTURED` twin this carries the raw underlying message (RFC §5.1.4).

accepts.description: Valid alternatives; this is what carries did-you-mean.

fixes.description: Remedies, ordered most-likely-first; an agent applying fixes[0] on the next attempt is the intended behavior. REQUIRED, and MAY be empty (an `UNSTRUCTURED` twin has no fixes yet).
